browser_benchmark.study_name: Browser MCP Head-to-Head Comparison (Playwright MCP vs CUL Browser MCP)
browser_benchmark.not_native_cua_note: Playwright MCP uses accessibility snapshots, not pure screenshots; this is NOT Native OpenAI Computer Use vs CUL.
browser_benchmark.cul_arm_commit_note: Browser-only MCP safeguard commit (CUL_MCP_BROWSER_ONLY=1); not automatically identical to later commits.
confounds_and_disclosures: Prompt contamination on b11_dense_90_grid_filter: shared goal text explicitly exposed CUL parameter name 'filter_query' to both arms (3/3 passed in both arms; Arm A used median 88,216 tokens vs CUL 164,300 tokens).
Arm A called browser_run_code_unsafe once on b12_opaque_canvas_click run 1 (page.mouse.click(199, 271)), so Arm A was not strictly accessibility-snapshot-only on all 36 runs.
CUL consumed ~40.0% more median tokens (176,506 vs 126,087) and +50.0% more median steps (4.5 vs 3.0) because each act bumps revision state and favors re-discovery.
CUL median wall time was ~1.5% slower (26.87s vs 26.48s), although cumulative total wall time across 36 runs was 936.84s vs 959.48s.
All 12 tasks were synthetic local HTML fixtures; results do not prove universal CUL superiority.

observation_size_comparison.subtitle: Estimated Observation Size — Not Actual API Token Usage
observation_size_comparison.sample_description: 12 browser fixtures x 5 headless runs (60 observations; min 23, max 664 on 90-button b11 grid)
caveats: Observation-size proxy only (round(text_length / 4)); NOT actual provider BPE token usage or total API task billing.
Multi-turn Codex runs (FIG-03) showed CUL used ~40% more median total tokens due to extra discovery steps and conversation context.
Dense uncapped surfaces (File Explorer uncapped 1,611; GitHub Trending uncapped 1,264) exceed static screenshot proxies, and Arabic text uses more BPE tokens per character.
